title: How can Nick Sirianni save his job? Eagles' path becomes more difficult without Lane Johnson - CBS Sports
description: Sirianni has his work cut out for him after his star right tackle called it a career
body:
Sirianni has his work cut out for him after his star right tackle called it a career
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        A 2-2 start to the season and the offensive woes that caused it increased the scrutiny on Philadelphia Eagles coach Nick Sirianni. Less than two years removed from a Super Bowl victory, Sirianni entered the 2026 campaign with little concern about his job security, but his seat warmed over the first four weeks and could reach scalding temperatures if he cannot reverse the Eagles' fortunes.The chances of Sirianni righting the ship took a significant blow on Tuesday when star offensive tackle Lane Johnson announced his sudden retirement from the NFL. Over the course of Johnson's career, Philadelphia ranked in the top three in offensive efficiency with him on the field and in the bottom six without him. His now permanent absence does not bode well for a unit that has looked bleak thus far in 2026.Regardless of Johnson's availability, Philadelphia owns a bottom-tier defense through four games. The Eagles rank 26th in scoring at 18.8 points per game and an even worse 29th in total offense at 269.8 yards per game. Despite boasting an elite running back in Saquon Barkley, the squad is a middle-of-the-pack rushing offense. And only two teams hold a lower EPA per pass.Last week, the Eagles made franchise history with their worst third-down execution in a single game. They went 0-for-12 on third down in the 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, which contributed largely to a late collapse in which they squandered a 10-point lead with less than four minutes to play.
The issues are not limited to just one facet of the offense. This was an issue last year, too, and now that it has become a trend, eyes are on Sirianni as the man responsible for fixing it.Struggles do not fall solely on SirianniIn Sirianni's defense, most coaching staffs would have found it difficult to move the ball against the star-studded Rams with the personnel available to him. Preventing Los Angeles' fourth-quarter comeback would have been a challenge considering the state of the defense, too. The following notable players were either inactive for Week 4 or suffered in-game injuries that prevented them from finishing the contest.RB Saquon Barkley: Suffered hamstring injury in Week 4WR DeVonta Smith: Inactive with hamstring injuryTE Dallas Goedert: Inactive with sprained MCLOG Cam Jurgens: Entered concussion protocol in Week 4OG Landon Dickerson: On injured reserve with knee bone bruiseOT Lane Johnson: Inactive due to personal reasons, later retiredLB Zack Baun: Inactive due to concussion protocolLB Jonathan Greenard: Suffered ankle injury in Week 4CB Quinyon Mitchell: Hyperextended knee in Week 4S Marcus Epps: Inactive with groin injuryThat does not even include the likes of Hollywood Brown, Tank Bigsby, Fred Johnson and other key non-starters who are on the shelf.
Sean Mannion hire has not panned outOnly two of Sirianni's three offensive coordinator hires have been fruitful. And since Kellen Moore left at the end of the 2024 season, the team has not been able to acquire a similarly high-caliber play-caller. There was hope that Sean Mannion would bring a fresh perspective this season in his first year as a coordinator, but the results thus far are underwhelming at best, and Sirianni has to own that.Jalen Hurts' own limitations at quarterback and the loss of A.J. Brown following his trade to the New England Patriots have been obvious. The Eagles need a coordinator who can mask those deficiencies like Moore and Shane Steichen did in their combined three seasons at the helm. The jury is still out on Mannion, but early returns are not nearly as promising as the team would have hoped.If Sirianni has to fire a second offensive coordinator in as many years, the focus will be trained even more closely on himself moving forward. And at the rate things are declining, it is uncertain whether he would even have time to make another change to his staff before his time is up.
How can Nick Sirianni save his job?Philadelphia's next three-game stretch is a grind. Each of its next three games comes against potential playoff teams in the Jacksonville Jaguars, Carolina Panthers and Dallas Cowboys. Considering the Eagles just dropped back-to-back games against that caliber of opponent, they will need to perform at a higher level in order to prevent an extended losing streak. Emerging from this stretch at 2-1 and thus holding a winning record through Week 7 would go a long way in keeping Sirianni's sixth year afloat.It will take a lot of behind-the-scenes work to achieve those results. Sirianni first has to figure out how to overcome the loss of Johnson. History suggests that the offense will be even worse in the weeks to come without its stalwart right tackle. He also needs to instill greater discipline throughout his roster after consecutive weeks with 10 penalties and after falling into a minus-three turnover deficit.And then there is the preparation aspect. The Eagles did not look ready in the slightest for the Chicago Bears' third-string quarterback, Case Keenum, two weeks ago. Sirianni's game-planning and CEO skills will be put to the test this week when the Eagles play in London. Not only is this international trip out of the ordinary, but it comes against a Jacksonville team that is deeply familiar with playing overseas. If the Eagles look lost in Week 5, much of that could come back to Sirianni.
The Eagles' coaching staff simply needs to keep its team competitive against tough competition and without a myriad of its best players. If Philadelphia comes out of this grueling stretch alive, then there will be enough opportunities on the other side to salvage this season or completely correct its course.

        It is no hyperbole to say that Zay Flowers has been one of the very best wide receivers in football this season. HIs 39.3% target per route run rate leads all receivers and is three points higher than Jaxon Smith-Njigba. His 6.29 yards per route run is two full yards better than Smith-Njigba and probably three yards better than any number you could reasonably expect a receiver to post over a full season. His 22.4 Fantasy points per game mark is sixth-best despite the fact that Week 4 was the first time this season he has played more than 33% of the offensive snaps. Now that he's fully healthy, we shouldn't even be discussing him; he should just be an obvious start. But, unfortunately, Lamar Jackson has an ankle injury, and Tyler Huntley is projected to start Week 5.Huntley has made 16 starts in his NFL career and has averaged 156.9 passing yards per game. He has 10 passing touchdowns and nine interceptions in those 16 starts. When all of the player props are out for the week, he will quite likely have the lowest projected passing yards. This is not exactly the offensive environment that produces top-20 wide receivers, much less top-5 options. Trying to build a projection around it isn't easy, but if we expect Huntley to throw 26 passes, and Flowers to be targeted on 30% of them, then you get a projection of eight targets. Huntley has completed 64.5% of his passes as a starter, so let's assume five catches. This year, Flowers has accounted for 49.6% of the Ravens' receiving yards when he's on the field; last year, it was 39.7%. If you split the difference, you get a yardage projection of 70 yards. Five catches for 70 yards with a mediocre chance at a touchdown is probably as good a guess as one could make, which makes Flowers a WR2 this week. In other words, you probably aren't getting the elite production you have so far, but you don't have to run away from him, even with Huntley at QB.Here is the rest of the Week 5 WR preview:

title: NFL penalties: League sets penalty record through Week 4 as tensions flare between teams, officials - CBS Sports
description: Coaches, players and officials have not seen eye to eye during a flag-happy start to the season
body:
Coaches, players and officials have not seen eye to eye during a flag-happy start to the season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:39 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        As important as officials are to the game of football, there is no world in which referees and their decisions should overshadow the players in NFL games. At times over the first four weeks of the 2026 season, it felt as though there was an imbalance in the focus on officials and the teams they moderated. Whether it was a product of poor calls or a lack of discipline from players, the NFL saw a record number of penalties in Weeks 1-4.According to ESPN, the 963 accepted penalties thus far are the most through Week 4 since play-by-play data became available in 1978. And the 271 accepted penalties in Week 4 alone were the second-most in any week during the play-by-play era.The following teams last week picked up double-digit infractions.TeamPenaltiesYardsChargers16130Browns1488Seahawks14150Ravens13131Jaguars13125Texans1390Jets1276Bengals11108Vikings1185Commanders1084Eagles1057Packers1068Twelve teams with at least 10 penalties is an astronomical number. The outlier-level volume of fouls goes beyond just Week 4, though. Perhaps the officials are doing exactly what is asked of them and honing in on points of emphasis. Maybe their quality of performance is at a low. Or possibly teams have been less disciplined in the early going this year than in seasons past. Any of the explanations is possible, or it could be a combination of all of them.Especially frustrating for teams is that the penalties are not just prevalent but also ill-timed.According to Warren Sharp, the number of penalties called on third or fourth down in the second half of games is the most in any Weeks 1-4 stretch since at least 2000. The volume of penalties inside the red zone is also a new high. And the 17 touchdowns nullified due to penalties are extremely out of proportion; only five were called back through Week 4 last year, and only four came off the board the year prior. The average over the previous decade was 8.3.These high-leverage calls halted drives and took points away from offenses. In fact, the uptick in penalties this year strictly impacts the offensive side of the ball. Sharp says the defensive penalty rate is lower in 2026 than in years past, and pass interference calls are below average.Tensions flare between players, coaches and officialsThe impact of the rise in penalties — and in some cases, the absence of calls — has been visible through players' and coaches' frustration with officials. In the New England Patriots' Week 4 win over the Buffalo Bills, coach Mike Vrabel received an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for arguing a pass interference flag that awarded the Bills a first-and-goal situation. Vrabel called referee Bill Vinovich "sensitive" for penalizing him for the use of profanity.
The NFL suspended two other officials for what it deemed "unprofessional conduct" toward players in Week 4.A league review of line judge Jeff Seeman's interaction with Trey McBride determined that the line judge used vulgar language at the Arizona Cardinals tight end. McBride initially pleaded for a pass interference penalty he thought should have been called on a third-down incompletion. CBS Sports sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala said McBride was heated in his plea for a penalty flag but did not use profanity toward the official. Seeman faces a two-game suspension.The league also issued a one-game suspension to referee Adrian Hill for an incident involving Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson. Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II shoved Wilson into the referee, who then fell backward to the ground. Wilson saw the referee take the tumble and extended his arms to help him up, but instead of taking the assistance, Hill stood up under his own power and began yelling at Wilson.The NFL Referees Association plans to challenge both suspensions."NFL officials have a responsibility to conduct themselves professionally on the field, and the actions in these incidents fell short of that standard," NFLRA executive director Scott Green said in a statement. "Accountability matters, but that should not result in discipline that is excessive or inconsistent with established precedent."

        The 2026 Major League Baseball postseason continued on Tuesday with a pair of NLDS Game 3s. In the early game, the Atlanta Braves hosted the Los Angeles Dodgers for what figures to be a pivotal game in the best-of-five series. The Braves' win in Game 2 evened the series at 1-1 and gave them home-field advantage the rest of the way. As well, the Braves had ace Chris Sale starting on full rest for Game 3 against Dodgers ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto.In the nightcap, the Milwaukee Brewers and San Diego Padres will go at it in Petco Park. With the Brewers up 2-0 in the series after a pair of white-knuckled contests in Milwaukee, the Padres find themselves in an elimination game and tasked with winning three games in a row over the best team in baseball in order to advance to the NLCS. Here are the final scores and schedule for Tuesday's crucial action:Dodgers 3, Braves 1 (box score); Dodgers up 2-1 in seriesBrewers at Padres, 9:30 p.m. ET (GameTracker); Brewers up 2-0 in seriesTo sum up all the NLDS Game 3 action, we're here to declare a winner and loser from each of the two Tuesday contests. You can find those declarations just below.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: The Dodgers' powerThe team that hits the most home runs had the overwhelming edge in a postseason game – or any game, for that matter – and that was indeed the case on Tuesday. The back-to-back World Series champion Dodgers are no stranger to such a thing. During the regular season, the Dodgers ranked second in MLB in slugging and tied for seventh in home runs. They were one of just nine teams in MLB to hit more than 200 homers during the 2026 season. No, hard-hitting DH Shohei Ohtani isn't himself at the plate right now, but the Dodgers are hardly a one-man power attack. This season, L.A. boasted four hitters who tallied at least 20 homers in 2026, seven who had at least 15, and nine who reached double figures in homers. In that game-turning top of the fourth of Game 3, Enrique Hernández, Dave Roberts' No. 9 hitter, did this to a 1-0 changeup from Sale with a runner on: 
That was a 2-0 Dodgers lead, and that was the 12th postseason home run of Hernández's Dodgers career. He trails just Max Muncy (18) and Corey Seager and Justin Turner (13) on the franchise's all-time list of career playoff homers. Hernández is now ahead of Duke Snider and Ohtani, who have 11 apiece. Two batters later, it was Freeman: On a night when Yamamoto was in peak form -- he allowed one run in seven innings with 10 strikeouts and only one walk -- and the bullpen did its job, that was more than enough. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Chris Sale, BravesGame 3 started off on a high note for Sale. Braves manager Walt Weiss was able to avoid using him in Game 2, which meant he was on full rest as he took the bump on Tuesday at Truist Park. He looked in peak form early, as he struck out the side in the first. He did the same in the second inning and thus became just the eighth pitcher in MLB postseason history to have six strikeouts in the first two innings. In the third, he hit 100 mph with his fastball – a ball to Shohei Ohtani. He did get spared some damage thanks to a highlight catch in left field by Mauricio Dubón. 
In the fourth, though, the Dodgers powered up at the expense of Sale and the Braves with a pair of home runs, including just the second by a left-handed batter – this one by former Brave Freddie Freeman – that Sale has allowed in all of 2026. As Inside Edge noted, it was just the second time in his entire career that Sale allowed a homer to a lefty on a fastball. The first was more than a decade ago. That uprising staked Sale's opposite number, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, to a 3-0 lead. By no means was Sale bad in Game 3 …
But three runs in five innings usually won't get it done against a pitcher like Yamamoto across the way. And indeed it didn't.

        Philadelphia Eagles six-time Pro Bowl offensive lineman Lane Johnson announced his immediate retirement from the NFL on Tuesday.Johnson was a surprise scratch from the Eagles' Week 4 lineup. The team listed him as inactive due to personal reasons and did not disclose specific details. His retirement comes just two days after he missed the 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.In his announcement, Johnson said it is "critical" that he focuses on his mental health at this moment.Over the final years of his career, Johnson opened up about his mental health struggles and revealed that he battled anxiety dating back to his freshman year of college in 2008. Earlier this year, he missed multiple training camp practices for personal reasons and said he felt the pull of off-field responsibilities weighing on him. In turn, Johnson said in August that 2026 would likely be his final year in the NFL.
Prior to his offseason announcement that he was trending toward retirement, a season-ending injury 10 games into the 2025 campaign raised questions about Johnson's long-term future in the league. He signed a contract extension in May 2025 that was set to keep him with the Eagles through 2027.
Johnson stands among the greatest offensive linemen of the 21st century. He is a two-time Super Bowl champion and five-time All-Pro, and the former No. 4 overall pick out of Oklahoma ends his career as an Eagles legend. He spent his entire career in Philadelphia and was a stalwart in the trenches for the franchise from 2013 through the third game of the 2026 campaign.The impact Johnson made on Philadelphia's offense was undeniable. Entering this season, the Eagles averaged 0.04 EPA per play with Johnson on the field (good for the third-best mark in the NFL) and -0.05 EPA per play without him (which made the offense the sixth-worst).Exemplifying why Johnson is widely considered to be one of the greatest right tackles in NFL history was the streak from Week 11 of the 2020 season to Week 9 in 2023, where he set a record for consecutive snaps without allowing a sack. Johnson kept his quarterbacks upright across a stretch of 1,405 straight pass-blocking snaps. During that timeframe, he set a separate record with 961 snaps without a knockdown.
Johnson is a strong candidate for enshrinement in the Pro Football Hall of Fame and will be eligible in five years.Teammates, coaches and others react to Lane Johnson's retirement

The second driver is a contender but is unlikely to win in the eyes of oddsmakers, but you'd win $200 after risking $100 if he does indeed pull off the upset.When you can bet on motor sports oddsThe racing schedule varies across NASCAR, F1 and IndyCar but there are usually weekly races with occasional breaks. NASCAR has multiple series, so there's usually at least one race across the series every weekend. F1 has a set calendar for the year with some breaks in between, but there are junior Formula racing series that might be going on in some of the gaps on the main circuit.Typically, the actual race will take place on a Sunday. There will be practice on either Thursday or Friday, with a qualifying event to set up the grid on either Friday or Saturday depending on the race schedule. Qualifying usually takes place the day before the race. Bettors can wager on qualifying outcomes as well, and those results will shift the race odds.Biggest races for motor sports bettingArguably, the biggest sporting event in the racing world is the Indianapolis 500, which is traditionally held on Memorial Day weekend. That's the premier IndyCar event.NASCAR has several big races, with the Daytona 500, a Crown Jewel event, regarded as the richest race on the circuit. The Coca-Cola 600 at Charlotte and the Brickyard 400 are also considered Crown Jewel events. Talladega Speedway is a widely known track thanks to the movie "Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby", but it is not a Crown Jewel event.Every F1 race has its unique twist. The tracks are different in each city, but Monaco is considered the biggest spectacle of the season. The race itself is somewhat mundane because there's little opportunity for drivers to pass each other. The British Grand Prix at Silverstone, the Italian Grand Prix at Monza and the Singapore Grand Prix are considered some marquee events on the F1 calendar. The Abu Dhabi Grand Prix is also a high-profile event as it is typically last on the calendar and could decide who wins the drivers championship and constructors championship. F1 has also added special events like Miami and Las Vegas.Types of bets and how motor sports betting works Like all sports betting markets, there are a variety of ways prospective bettors can wager on motor sports. Here's a look at some of them.Outright/To win oddsThis market is straightforward. Users are betting on which driver will win the event. There are also markets here for which team/constructor car will win the event, which will have multiple cars involved.Here are the odds to win the Singapore Grand Prix, taking place on October 11, 2026. Odds are courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook and are current as of October 6, 2026.Max Verstappen +225Andrea Kimi Antonelli +370Lando Norris +500Charles Leclerc +600Lewis Hamilton +600Placement/Top Finish oddsMotor sports betting offers users the ability to wager on drivers or teams having a certain placement or finishing within a certain range. For example, you can wager on drivers to place in the top 5 or top 10 of the event. You can do the same with teams/constructors.While it rarely occurs in racing, there's a possibility of multiple drivers tying for a position. In this case, there are  technically multiple winning bets. However, sportsbooks grade dead heats differently and the payouts can be different. If FanDuel declares a dead heat, half the stake is applied at the original odds and half the stake is lost. If there are more than two dead heats, the stakes are proportioned accordingly.Dual ForecastThis is where bettors can place a wager on which drivers will finish first and second. Both drivers must finish in the correct order for this wager to be paid out as a win. For example, you can wager on Max Verstappen and Lando Norris to finish first and second, respectively in a Dual Forecast market in F1 betting. However, if Verstappen finishes second and Norris finishes first, your bet will lose even though you did correctly pick the top two drivers for the race.Each Way BettingThis is not as common in motor sports but can be applied to racing betting. An each way bet basically places two wagers: a driver to win and to finish above another position. If the driver wins, both bets get paid out. The same applies for team bets in this market.Stage WinnerThis is prevalent in NASCAR and IndyCar, which has more laps than Formula One. You can bet on which driver or team will be in the lead after 25 laps, 50 laps, 100 laps and so on. These are the stages.Matchups/Head-to-HeadSportsbooks will put two drivers or two teams against each other, allowing bettors to choose which one will place higher. For teams, the bet is usually on the highest-placed driver for that particular team. This is one of the more popular F1 betting strategies. For example, if a market was being offered on F1 to see if Ferrari or Mercedes placed higher, the highest-placing Ferrari driver determines the result, even if both Mercedes drivers finish ahead of the second Ferrari driver. This means that bettors must consider both driver and car in situations like this.Group WinnerThis is offered in NASCAR. Sportsbooks will put a handful of drivers in groups and ask which will be the winner of the group.Top Car Make DriverThis is also specific to NASCAR, where you can bet on whether the winning driver will be in a particular car manufacturer, like Ford or Chevy. It's more applicable here since there are only two drivers on each F1 constructor, while car brands can span several NASCAR teams.Team of Race WinnerThis is similar to Outright Winner for drivers but applies to teams and constructors.Qualifying BetsBettors can wager on who will take pole position and which cars will be on pole. These are determined during qualifying racing, which typically takes place the day before the race. You can also bet on markets offering odds for who will finish in the top 5 or top 10 in qualifying, though these aren't necessarily  available for every race. The results of qualifying will often shift the race odds.Motor sports futures bettingFormula 1 bettingIn most cases, F1 futures usually apply to the next race. However, you can bet on season-long futures for F1 championship betting. The Drivers Championship is straightforward as it will be given to the driver who accumulates the most points over the season. The Constructors Championship takes into account the points for both team drivers. Only the top 10 finishers in each race score points, and those points are tallied over the season. The winning driver can be part of a constructors championship, but that's not always the case.NASCAR BettingNASCAR has different portions of the season. There are also different circuits like the Cup Series, the Xfinity Series and Truck Series. You can bet on marquee races for NASCAR in the futures market, and you can also wager on winners for these particular series.Below are DraftKings Sportsbook's odds for the NASCAR Cup Series Bank of America 400. Odds are current as of October 6.Kyle Larson +450Denny Hamlin +450Christopher Bell +500Chase Briscoe +550Tyler Reddick +750IndyCarThe major marquee futures market for IndyCar is the Indianapolis 500. Other than that race, there are season-long championship odds for the circuit.Can you parlay wagers in motor sports betting?While parlaying is generally not advised, as you don't get appropriate odds from sportsbooks that correspond to the actual chance of your bet winning, you are able to parlay outcomes in motor sports betting. While you can't pick multiple drivers to win an event in a parlay, you can pick multiple drivers to finish in the top 5 or top 10. You can also pick teams to finish in the top 5 or top 10.How to bet on motor sports live during a raceSportsbooks do offer live odds for motor sports, though this is likely a more prominent feature for NASCAR and IndyCar as opposed to F1. Driver and team odds will shift based on where they are in the grand scheme of the race. NASCAR and IndyCar allow for more leeway since there are more laps, while F1 can sometimes shift quickly towards one driver or team.Tips and strategies for how to bet on motor sportsDriver form does matter when it comes to racing, but the biggest predictor of success is usually how each team can adjust to conditions. Races can take place in all kinds of weather and team strategy can make or break the day. There are some teams that struggle to adjust, and bettors should know which teams those are before placing wagers. Historical track success often takes a back seat to current form. For example, Max Verstappen won the Canadian Grand Prix three years in a row and was a contender after starting second behind George Russell in 2025. Russell has had mixed results in Montreal historically but wound up winning the race after winning qualifying to take pole position.Longshots obviously don't usually win races, so they are better served as an inclusion in placement markets. You can usually back drivers who have had success on certain tracks or who have routinely finished just outside of a certain position market to break through eventually.Occasionally, a caution flag comes out when there's a crash on the track, which makes racing conditions hazardous for everyone. When this happens, there will be a safety car deployed, and all drivers must line up behind the safety car until the wreck is managed. There are different rules for each association and sometimes the race organizer makes a call in the moment, but usually, the race cannot end on a caution flag. If the wreck is too big to clear in a reasonable amount of time, the race will end despite the caution flag being signaled. Overtime doesn't really exist, but usually there will be at least one additional lap of racing should the fallout of the crash get removed in a timely manner and the safety car gets taken off the track.FAQCan you bet on motor sports?As long as you are of legal age in a state where sports betting is legitimate, you should be able to find a sportsbook which provides racing and motor sports odds.Who to bet on for the Indy 500?Because the Indy 500 typically takes place over Memorial Day weekend, you'll have to wait for a bit before placing wagers on who will win the signature event. Josef Newgarden won the Indy 500 in 2023 and 2024 but Alex Palou won in 2025 and is the reigning champion.Can you bet on SuperCross?SuperCross is a type of motorcycle racing. Some sportsbooks do offer SuperCross odds in certain states.Can you bet on motocross at DraftKings?DraftKings does provide SuperCross odds, which is a motocross competition, in select states. You must be of legal age and residing in those states to bet on motocross at DraftKings.How to bet on F1?All major sportsbooks have lines available for F1 races. Many of the same types of bets available for NASCAR races are available for F1 events.

Drake Maye ended his nightmare start to the season with 31 Fantasy points against them last week. A bigger part of it is that Stafford has Puka Nacua back. title: What's next for Wings? After Paige Bueckers' playoff debut, Dallas must shore up supporting cast - CBS Sports

body:
For the majority of last Friday night's winner-take-all Game 3 between the Dallas Wings and Golden State Valkyries, it seemed that the Wings were going to pull off a remarkable upset and advance to the semifinals for the first time since 2023. Instead, their 16-point lead kept slowly melting away until, with just over a minute left, it disappeared for good when Gabby Williams hit a go-ahead jumper. At the podium, shortly after a heartbreaking end to her sophomore campaign and postseason debut, Paige Bueckers was asked what stood out about this team and what they accomplished. "I think just our selfless nature and how much we enjoyed coming to work," Bueckers said, before pausing and burying her head in her towel, unable to hold back tears. After another All-WNBA-caliber season, Bueckers scored just 27 points on 27 shots in the final two games of the series while battling the Valkyries' relentless defense and a patellar tendinitis flare-up in her right knee that had limited her since the World Cup. Despite how things ended, the Wings' 2026 campaign should be seen as a success, both inside and outside the locker room. 
After winning 19 combined games in 2024 and 2025, the Wings made wholesale changes last offseason. They replaced Chris Koclanes with Jose Fernandez, signed Jessica Shepard and Alanna Smith in free agency and drafted Azzi Fudd with the No. 1 overall pick. In addition, they re-signed franchise stalwart Arike Ogunbowale. Back in the spring, there were real questions about how the new-look group was going to fare, especially given the organization's poor track record. How would Fernandez translate to the professional game after more than two decades at South Florida? Would Shepard and Smith be enough to shore up the frontcourt? Was Fudd, who is in a relationship with Bueckers, the right choice at No. 1? And did it make sense to bring Ogunbowale back into a crowded backcourt after the worst season of her career? Fernandez going on a lengthy postgame rant calling his players selfish after a 1-2 start didn't ease any of the concerns. But the Wings responded to Fernandez's challenge and won six of their next seven games, and by late July were sitting in fourth place thanks in large part to a breakout season from Shepard, who went on to win Most Improved Player and proved to be a far more impactful signing than Smith. 
The Wings stumbled on either side of the All-Star break, however, and in late August Fudd was ruled out for the season due to a knee injury that required surgery. By that point, the Wings were stuck in eighth place and had some work to do to fend off the expansion Portland Fire for the final playoff spot. While everyone expected they would, there was little hope for the rest of the season without Fudd. Even after they won seven of their final eight games to finish 27-17 -- a record-setting 17-win improvement on last season -- and earn the No. 7 seed, no one expected their first playoff appearance since 2023 to last long. A 24-point loss to the Valkyries in Game 1 only confirmed those thoughts. Ogunbowale would not let her team go down without a fight, however. She set the WNBA record for points in a playoff game with a heroic 45-point outing in Game 2, which included an absurd 3-pointer from deep in the corner to force overtime, and added another 30 points in Game 3 to nearly complete the upset. If she hadn't tweaked her groin in the fourth quarter of that game, which forced her to briefly go to the locker room, the Wings may still be playing right now. 
As it is, they're sitting at home, but with hope for the future. "I knew we were on the right trajectory when we got Paige," Ogunbowale said last Friday while an emotional Bueckers sat beside her. "Generational player. She willed us throughout the whole season, should be First Team All-WNBA. If not, I feel like that shit's rigged, because she's done everything for this team. I said it in signing back, I saw the vision."Season at a glanceRecord: 27-17 (No. 7 seed)Offensive rating: 111.3 (5th)Defensive rating: 106.4 (6th)Net rating: plus-6.8 (5th)Biggest strengthJump shootingNo team took more jumpers than the Wings this season, who fired 43.7 per game and 1,922 in total. They were a league-best 46.5% on 2-point jumpers and shot 34.8% from 3-point range, which ranked fifth in the league. All told, their 1.001 points per possession on jumpers ranked fifth. On an individual level, Paige Bueckers took 530 jumpers -- 69 more than any other player -- and among the 88 players who took at least 100 jumpers, no one shot better than her 47.2%. Arike Ogunbowale (367) and Azzi Fudd (268) ranked ninth and 21st, respectively, in jump shot attempts, and Fudd would have been even higher if not for a season-ending knee injury. When those jumpers were going in, the Wings were really tough to beat. 
Biggest weaknessPerformances against other playoff teamsThe Wings went 27-17 by beating up on lottery opponents. They were a remarkable 20-2 against the seven lottery teams, and both defeats -- against the Portland Fire and Phoenix Mercury -- were by a single point. By contrast, they were 7-15 against the seven other playoff teams, which obviously was not good enough and cost them a higher seed in the playoffs. Key free agentsAwak Kuier (restricted)Maddy Siegrist (restricted)Alysha Clark (unrestricted)Biggest question: How do they build out the supporting cast? The Wings don't have many free agents, but they still face an interesting offseason, in which they'll have to figure out which players they view as long-term fits alongside Bueckers and Fudd, and how they want to build out their supporting cast. As great as it was to win 17 more games this season, make the playoffs for the first time since 2023 and push the Valkyries to the limit, this team is still a few moves away from becoming a true contender. First and foremost, the Wings will have to address Kuier's restricted free agency. The former No. 2 overall pick returned to the WNBA this season after sitting out in 2024 and 2025, and though she didn't play much early on, became a key piece down the stretch. She is by far the best interior defender on the team, and after the All-Star break, led the league in blocks per game (2.6). Additionally, she shot 39% from 3-point range, and though her shot can be streaky, her ability to space the floor on the offensive end makes her a unique talent. Kuier is still only 25, and will certainly attract significant interest in free agency, but her restricted status means the Wings can match any offer she receives. 
The Wings committed over $1 million per year each to Smith, Shepard and Ogunbowale last offseason, but because Bueckers and Fudd are on rookie deals, they still have cap space to work with. Due to the new revenue sharing system, the exact salary cap figure for 2027 is still unclear, though we can assume it will be slightly higher than the 2026 figure of $7 million. The Wings currently have just under $5 million on the books for next season, which means they can re-sign Kuier at any cost, though doing so would limit their ability to fill out the rest of the roster unless they were able to trade one of Smith or Shepard. A congested 2027 cap sheet and less flexibility in free agency this offseason are small prices to pay to bring back a player as unique as Kuier, who is on the same timeline as Bueckers and Fudd, and retaining her should be the Wings' top priority. If that means that 2027 turns into a bridge year until Shepard and Ogunbowale's contracts are off the books (followed by Smith in 2028), that would not be the worst outcome. Especially when this group has already established itself as a playoff team and has two more first-round picks coming in this year's draft who could address some of their depth concerns, both now and in the future.  Draft outlookPicks Nos. 9, 13, 24 and 30After having the No. 1 overall pick in back-to-back drafts, the Wings will not have a lottery selection this year. They will, however, have two first-round picks -- No. 9, which is their own, and No. 13, which they got from the Las Vegas Aces via the NaLyssa Smith trade. In addition, the Wings will have two second-round picks, though those will be far less important. 
As currently constructed, the Wings have a crowded backcourt and frontcourt, but are very thin on the wing. Luckily for them, at least one of Maryland's Oluchi Okananwa or Ole Miss' Talaysia Cooper should still be on the board at No. 9. Either would be a welcome fit due to their athleticism and defensive playmaking, which would be a nice complement to the offensive skills of Bueckers and Ogunbowale. Their target at No. 13 would be more dependent on what happens in free agency. If they end up trading one of Shepard or Smith, or one of Kuier or Siegrist leaves in free agency, frontcourt depth would be a need. In that case, Chloe Kitts of South Carolina could be an option. It's also possible that the Wings don't have the roster spots or cap space to bring in two first-round picks and make a draft-and-stash selection at No. 13.
